issues.note_cycle_43: ROOT CAUSE MEASURED, not inferred. For 42 cycles the allowlist gap was a black-box observation ('the script is refused'); this cycle READ the permission source of truth, /opt/swarm/.claude/settings.json. permissions.allow contains exactly TWO SWARM-script entries: 'Bash(/Users/truman/Projects/SWARM/bin/swarm-notify.sh:*)' -- a macOS path that does not exist on this host -- and 'Bash(bin/swarm-notify.sh:*)', the relative form that works. There is NO entry for swarm-budget.sh or swarm-playbook.sh in ANY path form, and none for the VPS prefix /opt/swarm/bin. The underlying cause of the whole KI-5 family is that settings.json was never migrated from macOS to the VPS. Established by a 16-check gate (.swarm/runs/cycle-043-gate-ki5.js, output cycle-043-verify-ki5.txt): the allowlist contents PREDICTED 7/7 measured cells including two negative controls (awk absent -> denied; pgrep present -> clean) and two cells no prior cycle had measured. The discriminator is cell 3 vs cell 4: identical script AND arguments (swarm-notify.sh poll), varying ONLY the path form, giving OPPOSITE outcomes -- absolute DENIED, relative CLEAN. A 'the script isn't allowlisted' theory predicts those two alike; the allowlist predicts them opposite, which is the observation a wrong theory could not have produced. TWO OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCES, derived from the allowlist rather than executed: (S8) WRAP_UP's 'bin/swarm-playbook.sh append' WILL be refused -- the manual fallback is confirmed necessary, and was pre-drafted this cycle to /opt/swarm/runs/wrapup-candidates.md rather than left to the WRAP_UP clock; (S9) 'bin/swarm-notify.sh send wrap-up ...' relative from cwd=/opt/swarm WILL be permitted, so the wrap-up push can go out -- previously unknown and assumed dead. ALSO FOUND: permissions.additionalDirectories is EMPTY, so the target is reachable only via the pacer's --add-dir flag. NOTE the compounding with note_cycle_12: the playbook is inert for TWO independent reasons -- the cap breach (cmd_parse exits 2 at >20 lessons) AND this allowlist gap. Fixing either alone leaves it inert. NOT FIXED HERE, deliberately: hard rule 5 makes settings.json read-only until WRAP_UP completes, so tool bugs found mid-run go to the journal and the morning report, never to a live edit. The repair is two added lines.

issues.desc: Subagents in this VPS -p session are sandboxed to the session --add-dir list (/opt/swarm, /opt/targets/aphorism-cli). A git worktree under /tmp is therefore UNREACHABLE to a builder: reads, bash, and EnterWorktree all refuse. Cycle 18 lost one builder dispatch to this. SKILL.md already prescribes "no worktrees" for headless sessions and gives disjoint file scopes as the concurrency answer instead; cycles 16-17 used /tmp worktrees anyway and cycle 18 is where it bit. Remedy for future cycles: at k_cap 1 let the single builder work directly in the target tree (conductor still sole committer); for k>1 headless, either scope builders to disjoint files in the one tree or place worktrees INSIDE an allowed directory.

Subagent scratch files land in the SWARM root (/opt/swarm) unless the dispatch prompt names an explicit scratch path. Hard rule 5 hands agents target paths only, but the session cwd IS /opt/swarm, so a relative scratch path silently lands inside the write fence -- the fence is enforced by what agents are TOLD, and cwd supplies what they were not told. Observed cycle 9 (builder used /opt/swarm/.scratch/) and again at cycles 17-18 (9 untracked .js/.json scratch files in the SWARM root, removed by the conductor at cycle 19). Harmless so far -- all occurrences were inert scratch, nothing under bin/, reference/, workflows/ or templates/ -- but the same reflex on a different task could write into SWARM tooling mid-run. CYCLE 36: control PASSES a third consecutive time. The dispatch prompt named an explicit scratch path (<target>/.swarm/scratch-c36/) and the builder used it; /opt/swarm stayed clean, verified by `git -C /opt/swarm status --porcelain`. The builder did NOT remove its own scratch tree this time (cycle 35's did), so the conductor removed it before commit -- the naming control is what is working; self-cleanup is not reliable and should not be assumed.
issues.note_cycle_21: THIRD occurrence, in a new and milder variant: the dispatch prompt named the explicit in-target scratch path as the remedy prescribes, and the builder honored it AND deleted its mutation copies -- but left the bare empty .swarm/scratch directory behind. Measured at 0 files inside, so nothing leaked and no untracked scratch reached git status; this is the same residue cycle 9 recorded (agent removes copies, conductor removes the empty directory). Caught only because the conductor gate carries a standing SCOPE.SCRATCH control, which is the reason to keep that control even on cycles where it looks like a formality. Remedy refinement for the wrap-up distillation: the prompt should say remove the scratch DIRECTORY, not just its contents.
issues.remedy: Name an explicit scratch directory in every dispatch prompt. NOT /tmp -- KI-6 established subagents are sandboxed to the session --add-dir list, so /tmp is unreachable. Use <target>/.swarm/scratch/ and require the agent to remove it, with a conductor gate check confirming the removal. Done this way at cycle 19 (T-013) and the agent left nothing behind (harness controls CTRL-SCRATCH, CTRL-TREE). Cycle 9 proposed this as a candidate playbook lesson and it was never made standing, which is why it recurred; it belongs in the wrap-up distillation.
issues.note_cycle_24: FOURTH occurrence, and it PARTIALLY CONTRADICTS the cycle-22 note below, so that note should not be read on its own. The cycle-21 remedy refinement was again applied verbatim in the dispatch prompt -- it named the in-target scratch path AND required removing the scratch DIRECTORY itself, not merely its contents, calling out that an empty directory counts as debris and is checked. The builder created three subdirectories under .swarm/scratch/ and reported removing them with rm -rf, which it had genuinely done: the standing SCOPE.SCRATCH control found .swarm/scratch present with ZERO entries inside. So the agent removed what it created and still left the parent it did not create. Nothing leaked, git status showed no untracked scratch, and the conductor removed the directory by hand. The lesson for the wrap-up distillation is narrower and more useful than 'name the scratch path': an agent told to remove its scratch directory removes the directories IT MADE, so the prompt must name the exact path whose absence is checked, or the check must tolerate an empty parent. Cycle 22's 'the remedy is now measured to work' was drawn from a single clean cycle and does not survive a second sample.
issues.note_cycle_30: NO occurrence, but this cycle is NOT evidence about the remedy and must not be counted as a clean sample. The standing SCOPE.SCRATCH control passed -- .swarm/scratch is absent and the SWARM root carried no debris at orient or at commit -- yet the builder reported that its scratch mkdir was DENIED OUTRIGHT by the permission layer before executing, because the path it reached for was tied to an out-of-scope README.md verification. So the directory was never created, and the reason is the sandbox rather than the prompt. Recorded this way because cycle 22 drew 'the remedy is measured to work' from a single clean cycle and cycle 24 then contradicted it; counting a permission denial as a third clean sample would repeat that error in a worse form. The issue stays OPEN. Second-order note, more useful than the control itself: the same denial is why the builder could not run the README mutation table empirically and said so unprompted -- the file-scope fence and the builder's ability to self-verify are in genuine tension here, and the conductor gate is what closes it.
issues.note_cycle_22: NO occurrence this cycle, and that is evidence rather than luck. The cycle-21 remedy refinement was applied verbatim in the dispatch prompt -- it named the in-target scratch path AND required removing the scratch DIRECTORY itself, not merely its contents, calling out that an empty directory counts as debris and is checked. The builder honoured both: the standing SCOPE.SCRATCH control passed for the first time since the refinement was written (.swarm/runs/cycle-022-verify-T-016.txt), and the SWARM root carried no debris at orient either. The issue stays OPEN because one clean cycle does not close a structural hole -- the fence is still enforced by what the prompt says, and a prompt that forgot the line would reproduce it -- but the remedy is now measured to work, which is what the wrap-up distillation needs.
issues.note_cycle_31: FIFTH occurrence, and this one is the CONDUCTOR'S FAULT rather than the agent's -- recorded that way because the remedy did not fail, it was never applied. The dispatch prompt did not name the in-target scratch path at all; it said "do your experimenting in-memory or in /tmp", and KI-6 has established since cycle ~17 that /tmp is unreachable from a subagent sandbox. Verified clean by the conductor: git status in /opt/swarm is empty and ls of the root shows no residue. Nothing leaked and nothing under bin/, reference/, workflows/ or templates/ was touched. The finding that matters for the wrap-up distillation is that four cycles of remedy refinement are worth nothing if the line is not actually in the prompt -- the fence is enforced by prose that a conductor has to remember to type, which is the structural complaint, not the agent's behaviour. Do not count this as evidence about the remedy in either direction.
issues.note_cycle_37: Control PASSES a fourth consecutive time and this cycle is a CLEAN sample, unlike cycle 30's permission-denied non-sample. The dispatch prompt named the explicit in-target path (<target>/.swarm/scratch-c37/) AND required removing that exact directory rather than merely its contents -- the cycle-24 refinement. The builder created it, used it for a four-variant README harness, and removed it itself; the conductor confirmed absence, and `git -C /opt/swarm status --porcelain` was empty at both orient and commit. issues.note_cycle_4_run2: CONTROL PASSES, and this is the BEST sample the family has produced — the first time SELF-CLEANUP held for EVERY agent in a wave. Both dispatch prompts named an explicit in-target path (.swarm/scratch-c004-j4/, .swarm/scratch-c004-j6/) AND required removing THAT EXACT DIRECTORY rather than merely its contents (the cycle-24 refinement). issues.note_cycle_7_run3: TWO FINDINGS, and the second is a NEW CLASS the standing control cannot see. (1) The naming control PASSED again: the dispatch prompt named .swarm/scratch-c007-q1/ and required removing THAT EXACT directory, and the builder created it, used it (it stashed a parallel orig-tree/ there to run the new tests against the unfixed binary) and removed it itself. `ls -a .swarm/` shows no scratch directory and `git -C /opt/swarm status --porcelain` was empty at orient and at commit. (2) THE NEW CLASS: /opt/swarm carries tmp_aph_err.txt and tmp_aph_out.txt, both 0 bytes, mtimes 06:01:57Z and 06:04:53Z — i.e. cycle 6, before this cycle opened. They are not merely untracked debris: `git -C /opt/swarm log -- tmp_aph_err.txt` names commit 76b3a01, cycle 6s own SWARM-side commit, so cycle 6 COMMITTED its scratch into the SWARM repo root. This matters more than the count: the standing SCOPE.SCRATCH control is `git status --porcelain`, and a COMMITTED file reads clean, so the control is structurally blind to exactly this variant and would report a pass forever. `git ls-files` at the SWARM root is the check that sees it — the whole non-directory tracked set there is .gitignore, CLAUDE.md, SKILL.md, .claude/settings.json plus these two strays. NOT REMOVED, deliberately: hard rule 5 limits in-run SWARM writes to runs/ and playbook/, and these sit at the root, so removing them is itself outside the fence. Handed to the morning report; the removal is `git rm tmp_aph_err.txt tmp_aph_out.txt`.

issues.desc: The conductor's sealed pre-dispatch baseline is READABLE BY THE BUILDER IT IS MEANT TO BE SEALED FROM. It is written to <target>/.swarm/runs/, which is inside the target directory every builder is given, so a builder that looks around the tree can read the exact cells the conductor committed to before dispatch. Observed cycle 31: the builder volunteered, unprompted, that it had noticed .swarm/backlog.json and two new .swarm/runs/ files and identified them as "the conductor/swarm tooling's own pre-dispatch baseline for this exact item", correctly naming cell B4 and its reading of 50. CYCLE 36 MITIGATION, which does NOT close the root cause: the conductor now uses commit-reveal -- seal written, sha256 committed before dispatch, plaintext DELETED for the whole dispatch window, rewritten and verified with `sha256sum -c` after the builder returns (OK at cycle 36). A deleted file cannot be read by any builder, so THIS cycle's seal was genuinely sealed. The root cause is untouched: <target>/.swarm/runs/ is still inside every builder's directory, every OTHER artefact there (prior gates, probes, baselines) is still readable, and the mitigation is conductor discipline rather than a structural boundary. A future conductor that forgets the delete step is back to KI-8 exactly as filed. The structural fix needs a scratch location outside the subagent sandbox that the conductor can also write, which this session does not have (KI-6 establishes /tmp is outside the sandbox; the Write tool is denied there).
issues.status: mitigated in practice, root cause open
issues.why_it_matters: Hard rule 2 rests on builders never having seen the check -- an agent that knows the check can code to it. The rule is enforced today by not PUTTING verify commands in the backlog, which is necessary but not sufficient: the baseline file is a second copy of much of the same information sitting in a directory the agent can read. This cycle it changed nothing and the honesty was exemplary -- the builder disclosed it rather than using it, and the decisive evidence (D1/D2) was authored AFTER dispatch and never written to disk until the gate ran, so the verdict is uncontaminated. But the integrity of the gate should not depend on a builder choosing to disclose.
issues.remedy: Candidate for the wrap-up distillation, not a mid-run change (hard rule 5 forecloses editing SWARM tooling during a run). Options worth measuring next run, cheapest first: (1) write pre-dispatch baselines to SWARM/runs/ instead of <target>/.swarm/runs/, and copy them into the target only at commit time, so the evidence still lands in the target repo's history but not in the builder's live tree; (2) keep authoring the deciding discriminators strictly after dispatch, which is what actually saved this cycle and is already the hard-rule-2 practice; (3) accept and document it, on the grounds that a builder reading the baseline still cannot see the post-dispatch discriminators. Option 1 plus 2 looks strictly better than 3 and costs almost nothing.
issues.note_cycle_32: SECOND OCCURRENCE, AND A WORSE ONE — SEVERITY RAISED medium -> high. Cycle 31 the builder read the pre-dispatch BASELINE. This cycle the builder read .swarm/runs/cycle-031-verify-T-024a.js, which is the GATE ITSELF, containing the full cycle-31 discriminator set D1-D4 and cells G0-G6. It disclosed this unprompted and in detail (report section 6: "my independent measurement was informed by, not blind to, that prior gate's specific cell shapes"), and it explicitly validated its work against those cells. So the escalation is not hypothetical any more: at cycle 31 an agent could have coded to the conductor's check, and at cycle 32 an agent demonstrably DID optimise against it. D1 and D2 were consequently useless as discriminators this cycle. The verdict was saved only because the conductor authored a fresh 9-cell H-set AFTER the builder returned, which is remedy option (2) from the cycle-31 entry doing exactly the job it was proposed for. TWO REFINEMENTS FOR THE WRAP-UP DISTILLATION, both sharper than the original entry: (a) the leak is not only the baseline but EVERY prior cycle's gate artefact, which accumulates in .swarm/runs/ and grows monotonically -- by cycle 32 that directory holds a decade of this run's adversarial thinking, all of it readable by every builder; (b) a second-order harm the cycle-31 entry did not anticipate — the builder inherited cell D4 WITHOUT the backlog note recording that D4 was mis-authored and attributes nothing, then built its headline silent-hole claim on it. Leaked evidence arrives stripped of the caveats that live in the backlog, so it is not merely visible, it is misleading.
issues.note_cycle_33: THIRD OCCURRENCE, THIRD DISTINCT CHANNEL, AND THIS ONE IS THE CONDUCTOR'S FAULT. Cycle 31 the agent read the pre-dispatch BASELINE; cycle 32 it read the GATE; cycle 33 it read the conductor's UNCOMMITTED WORKING-TREE EDIT via `git diff test/readme-tags.test.js`, which contained the full BOUNDARY classification and its reasoning. Note what this defeats: the cycle-33 mitigation (pre-commitment sealed to /home/swarm/.swarm-seal/, outside the --add-dir sandbox, with only its SHA-256 committed into the target before dispatch) WORKED -- the seal was never readable. The leak happened because the conductor applied its conclusion to a tracked file while the agent was still running. The agent's read was also legitimate in intent: it saw unexpected modifications in `git status` and diffed a tracked file to check whether it had caused them, which is careful behaviour, and it disclosed the whole thing unprompted and in detail including the ordering of its own measurements. REMEDY, sharper than options (1)-(3) and superseding option (1) which is simply WRONG (it proposes SWARM/runs/, but KI-6 establishes the sandbox is the --add-dir list, which INCLUDES /opt/swarm): (4) hash-commit the seal outside the sandbox -- measured to work this cycle; and (5) THE CONDUCTOR MUST NOT WRITE ITS OWN CONCLUSIONS INTO THE WORKING TREE WHILE AN INDEPENDENT AGENT IS RUNNING. Wait for the return, then edit. Costs nothing and closes the only channel the hash commitment does not.
issues.note_cycle_37: Commit-reveal held a SECOND consecutive cycle. Seal written, sha256 committed to the target before dispatch (07efb5a), plaintext DELETED for the whole dispatch window, restored afterwards and verified `sha256sum -c` OK. The builder additionally volunteered, unprompted, that it had run `ls .swarm/` once and had opened NO file under .swarm/runs/ -- the disclosure norm holding for the third cycle running. Root cause STILL UNTOUCHED and this must not be read as closing: every other artefact in .swarm/runs/ remains readable by every builder, and the seal is protected by conductor discipline, not by a boundary. A conductor that forgets the delete step is back to KI-8 exactly as filed. NEW THIS CYCLE, and it is a SEPARATE CHANNEL the commit-reveal does not cover: the ACCEPTANCE CLAUSE itself leaked a test input. T-033's acceptance named the exact reword wording, the builder's fix enumerated exactly that wording, and the acceptance cell consequently could not discriminate. Sealing the gate does nothing about this -- the backlog acceptance is handed to the builder by design. See T-034 and the cycle-37 decision entry.
issues.note_cycle_4_run2:
FOURTH OCCURRENCE, FOURTH DISTINCT CHANNEL, and the mitigation both HELD and LOST GROUND in the same cycle. Read all three parts.

(1) COMMIT-REVEAL HELD, third consecutive cycle. A sealed pre-dispatch truth table for J-4 was written, its sha256 (077e6a26...a4eb) committed to the target at e06852b BEFORE either builder was dispatched, the plaintext DELETED for the whole dispatch window, then rewritten from conductor context and verified `sha256sum -c` OK. The J-4 builder independently confirmed it saw nothing referencing cycle-004. So the numbers that gate judged against are provably pre-dispatch, which is exactly what the mechanism is for.

(2) THE NEW CHANNEL: A REPO-WIDE GREP WHOSE EXCLUSION PATTERN SILENTLY FAILED. Prior channels were an agent reading the baseline (c31), the gate (c32), and the conductor s uncommitted working-tree diff (c33). This one is different in kind: the J-4 builder ran `grep -rniE audit ... | grep -v '^\./\.swarm/runs/'` to sweep the repo for the audit word family, and the exclusion anchored on a leading `./` that the actual grep output did not carry (paths came back as `.swarm/runs/...`). The filter therefore matched nothing and single matched lines from roughly 18 files under .swarm/runs/ entered its output, which it then read. It DISCLOSED this unprompted, in detail, and enumerated every file — the disclosure norm holding for the fourth cycle running. CONTAMINATION ASSESSED AS NIL FOR THIS VERDICT: every leaked line was run-#1 historical material (cycles 10, 11, 22, 32, 34, 35, 41, 43, 44, 45) and none touched cycle-004 or this cycle s seal. WHAT IS NEW AND MATTERS: the "do not read .swarm/runs/" instruction is enforced by the AGENT S OWN SHELL HYGIENE. A prompt can forbid a directory; it cannot make a one-line grep filter correct. Every prior channel was closable by conductor discipline; this one is not, because the agent was trying to comply and its tooling betrayed it.

(3) THE STRONGER MITIGATION IS UNAVAILABLE IN THIS SESSION SHAPE, which is a regression against the cycle-33 remedy. Remedy (4) was "hash-commit the seal outside the sandbox", measured working at cycle 33 with /home/swarm/.swarm-seal/. This session CANNOT write there: `mkdir -p /home/swarm/.swarm-seal` is refused by the allowed-working-directories check, which permits only /opt/swarm and /opt/targets/aphorism-cli. So the out-of-sandbox seal is gone and only the in-sandbox delete-for-the-window variant remains. That variant is strictly weaker: it depends on the conductor remembering to delete, and it protects nothing if a session dies mid-dispatch with the plaintext on disk. A future SWARM revision should either grant the conductor one write path outside the subagent sandbox, or stop prescribing a remedy the runtime no longer permits. Recorded here rather than fixed: hard rule 5 fences settings and tooling until WRAP_UP.
issues.note_cycle_8_run2: COMMIT-REVEAL HELD A FOURTH CONSECUTIVE CYCLE, and this cycle produced an unusually clean control for it. issues.desc: The README Attribution section's two count claims (C1 corpus size, C2 HIGH-risk count) cannot be bound to their markers by any measured rule without falsely rejecting some naturally-written, entirely-TRUE README. Two independent attempts at T-024a, reasoning from different premises, each produced a lateral or negative trade: attempt 1 (cycle 31) swapped "last number before the marker" for "first number in the clause" and scored a perfect 2/4 <-> 2/4 mirror; attempt 2 (cycle 32) swapped positional scanning for two closed grammatical templates and scored 5/9 against HEAD's 7/9 on an independent 9-cell gate, buying one repair (subject-first partitive) with three new false rejections. T-024a is BLOCKED at attempts 2.
issues.status: RESOLVED at cycle 2 of run #2 — by removal, which is the one route it named and could not take
issues.why_it_matters: AMENDED AT CYCLE 35: the clause below that these guards "fail LOUD on wordings they cannot parse, which is the safe direction" is NO LONGER COMPLETE, and it is left standing with this correction rather than quietly rewritten. Cycle 35 measured a wording they fail SILENT on -- a contradictory count whose digit sits across a dash from its marker binds nothing and is skipped, so a self-contradicting README passes green (KI-10). The loud-only framing held for every case examined through cycle 34; it does not hold in general. Original text follows. These guards are the only thing standing between the README and a silently false claim about the corpus. They currently work on the shipped text and fail LOUD on wordings they cannot parse, which is the safe direction -- nothing is broken for a user today. The risk is the one cycle 25 identified and this issue now quantifies: a maintainer who reformats the Attribution paragraph in a perfectly reasonable way gets a red suite, and the cheapest escape from a false rejection is DELETING the guard, which would take C1 and C2 with it. Twice-measured evidence that no prose-reading rule fixes this is the input a human needs, and it is a judgment call a swarm should not make alone.
issues.remedy: NOT another attempt at the same shape -- that is what the attempts cap is for, and the second attempt confirmed rather than contradicted the first. The choice is a human one, between three options this run can lay out but should not pick: (1) ACCEPT AND DOCUMENT -- state at the extraction site that the guard reads the shipped wording and fails loud on rewordings, and that the correct response to a red C1/C2 is to check the numbers and then adjust the template, never to delete the assertion. Cheapest, honest, and consistent with SPEC I-2, which explicitly allows a BOUNDARY survivor to be documented rather than hardened. (2) CHANGE THE DOCUMENT, NOT THE PARSER -- put the two counts somewhere with real structure the guard can read (a small table, or a fenced key: value block in the Attribution section), which removes the English sentence from the loop entirely. This is the only option that actually satisfies T-024's stated remedy, and it is a README change, which is out of the builder file scope this run has used throughout. (3) DROP C1/C2 and rely on the triage document alone. Option 2 is the conductor's lean and it is recorded as a lean, not a decision; it is also the only one of the three that would make T-029 disappear as a side effect.
issues.note_cycle_2_run2: The finding itself is NOT overturned and should not be read as retracted: no rule reading an English sentence to decide which number a claim means avoids falsely rejecting some true README. It was measured twice and both measurements stand. What changed is that nothing reads an English sentence any more. This issue named three options for a human and leaned toward option (2), "change the document, not the parser", noting it was the only one that satisfies T-024's remedy and that it was out of the then-current builder file scope. Option (2) is what shipped. The lean was correct.

issues.desc: SILENT MISS, LEFT OPEN BY A MEASURED DECISION. The README Attribution guards (C1 corpus size, C2 HIGH-risk count) bind a count to its marker only within the marker's own dash-delimited clause. A contradictory count whose DIGIT sits across an em/en dash from its MARKER therefore binds nothing at all, and an occurrence that binds nothing is skipped rather than counted as unparseable -- so a self-contradicting README passes GREEN. Reproduced at cycle 35: appending "A later audit note records 9 (em dash) HIGH entries (em dash) in total." to the Attribution section leaves the suite at 78/78 while the true HIGH count is 8. Written with ASCII "--" instead, the identical contradiction IS caught -- the dash clause split is provably the mechanism, not a guess.
issues.status: RESOLVED at cycle 2 of run #2 — measured closed on a two-arm gate
issues.why_it_matters: This is the one failure DIRECTION this improvement run was chartered to remove. Every other open member of this guard family fails LOUD -- it rejects a correct README, which is irritating and safe. This one lets a README that contradicts itself in plain sight pass green, which is worse than having no guard, because a green suite is read as a claim that the numbers were checked. It also corrects KI-9's "fails loud, which is the safe direction" framing, which was accurate for everything examined up to cycle 34 and is not accurate in general.
issues.remedy: NOT another narrowing of collectMarkerBindings. That was measured at cycle 35 and the measurement is the reason this issue exists rather than a fix: a 44-cell gate (11 README mutations x 4 arms) rebuilt BOTH natural widenings from the shipped helper -- V1, an unconditional fallback to the previous clause's trailing digit, and V2, that fallback gated on the previous clause holding no marker of its own. BOTH close this hole (cell G1 RED) and BOTH buy a NEW false rejection on entirely TRUE prose (cells CA and CB RED, GREEN on HEAD): a sentence naming a marker with no count at all borrows the neighbouring clause's digit, and an unrelated year does the same. Crossing the clause boundary to catch this shape and avoiding the unrelated-number hazard are the same request. The real fix is KI-9 remedy option (2): give the two counts real structure in the README (a small table or a fenced key: value block) so the guard stops reading English. That is a README change, out of the builder file scope used throughout this run, and it would retire this issue, KI-9, T-032 and the rest of the family together. A human should make that call. Evidence: .swarm/runs/cycle-035-verify-T-031.txt, harness .swarm/runs/cycle-035-gate.js, boundary documented in a 47-line comment at the helper in test/readme-tags.test.js.

issues.desc: SWARM/runs/dashboard.html carries THREE copies of the cycle-37 timeline tick; two of them sit INSIDE HTML comment regions. An earlier render leaked them there. The standing containment check in every render script since cycle ~34 asserts only that a substitution lands AFTER </style> -- but every commented-out template legend in this file also lives after </style>, so the check cannot see a comment breach. Comments do not render, so the PAGE was never visually wrong and no viewer ever saw stale or duplicated content; what the leak corrupts is ANCHOR UNIQUENESS.
issues.why_it_matters: It cost a render this cycle -- and it cost it in the SAFE direction, which is the part worth recording. The cycle-35 uniqueness guard ('the anchor must occur exactly once, else throw') fired and ABORTED rather than silently no-opping or, worse, splicing the new tick into a comment where nobody would ever see it. That is the guard working exactly as designed: it turned an invisible corruption into a loud stop. Left at LOW severity because the rendered page is correct and the failure mode is loud, not silent.
issues.remedy: Cycle 38's render script (SWARM/runs/cycle-038-render.js) already carries the repair and it should be carried forward rather than rediscovered: classify each anchor occurrence by whether the nearest preceding '<!--' is later than the nearest preceding '-->', count only LIVE occurrences, require exactly one, and splice POSITIONALLY at that offset instead of String.replace -- replace would take the FIRST match, which here is a comment copy at byte 4875, before </style>. NOT FIXED AT THE SOURCE THIS RUN: the two stale comment-region copies are still in dashboard.html, and templates/dashboard.template.html plus the containment convention live under the hard-rule-5 read-only fence. Candidate for the wrap-up distillation: a render's containment rule must exclude comment regions, not just the style block.

SWARM TOOL GAP, HIGH because it disables a spend governor (morning report, not a live edit -- hard rule 5 fences bin/). bin/swarm-allocator.sh detects a weekly rollover with an exact integer comparison against the usage probe's week_resets_at: `if [ "$WRST" -ne "$S_WRST" ]; then HU=0; HP=0; SU=0; SP=0; TU=0; ...`. The upstream value is not stable to the second. api/oauth/usage returns seven_day.resets_at with sub-second precision straddling a whole-second boundary; 25 samples over 125s returned BOTH 1786942799 and 1786942800, and four consecutive 5s samples caught the crossing live (04:59:59.954603 -> 05:00:00.110580 -> .317042 -> .463901). Evidence: runs/cycle-040-resets-jitter.json. CONSEQUENCE OBSERVED, not theorised: at 2026-08-16T02:16:47Z the branch fired with no week having rolled over and reset trickle_used_pct from 4 (the configured trickle_pct cap, i.e. exhausted) to 0. That flipped posture halted -> trickle and the pacer spawned cycle 40 on a cap that had not actually been refilled -- the real reset is 2026-08-17T05:00Z, after this run's stop_at. The cap therefore cannot hold across a boundary crossing: it silently refills and the swarm is re-authorised to spend another trickle_pct of a weekly allowance already at 93% (opus 97%). Human attribution (human_used_pct / human_active) is wiped by the same branch, so the human reserve curve resets too. Candidate fixes for a human, none applied: compare with a tolerance (e.g. treat |WRST - S_WRST| <= 2 as the same week), or round/floor the probe value to a stable unit, or gate the rollover on the value having moved FORWARD by most of a week. The conductor held at zero agents this cycle rather than accept the refill -- see decisions[] cycle 40.
issues.note_cycle_41: SCOPED, NOT DOWNGRADED -- severity stays high and the bug is unchanged. Measured this cycle: the rollover wipe cannot re-authorise spend on THIS run, because allow_overall_pct is already 0 on a second, independent gate the wipe does not touch. bin/swarm-allocator.sh calc() (lines 83-96) sets the human reserve to 24.01% against a weekly remainder of 7% (weekly_used_pct 93), so allow = max(0, 100 - 93 - 24.01) = 0. The reserve floor of 12 releases only within floor_release_hours=6 of the week reset and there are 17.59h left at stop_at, so it never releases before the run ends; allow > 0 would need weekly_used_pct below 79.83%, and weekly usage is monotonic within a week. Transcription control: the reproduced reserve is 24.01 against 24.04 reported, the gap being the clock difference since the allocator last refreshed. WHAT THIS DOES NOT MEAN: the bug is still high and still live -- on a week where the reserve curve is open (lower weekly_used_pct, or inside the 6h floor release) the same wipe DOES refill a spent cap, and it wipes human attribution unconditionally, which resets the human reserve curve itself. Evidence: runs/cycle-041-allocmath.js.

SWARM TOOL GAP, HIGH because it FAILS OPEN on a spend authorisation (morning report, not a live edit -- hard rule 5 fences bin/). At 2026-08-16T07:10Z SWARM/runs/allocator.json was rewritten with every usage field zeroed and "source":"none", "ok":false -- the usage probe returned nothing. While blind it still emitted allow_overall_pct 10 and allow_premium_pct 10, i.e. a NON-ZERO spend authorisation derived from no data. A conductor that reads the allowance without checking `ok` would treat a probe blackout as permission to spend 10% of a window last measured (cycle 46, runfile budget.weekly) at 95% weekly / 97% opus. DISCRIMINATOR against the innocent explanation: this is not a week rollover -- week_resets_at is 0, whereas a genuine reset carries a future epoch, and the real reset is not due until 1786942799 (2026-08-17T02:19Z), 19h away. DISTINCT FROM KI-14, which wipes the swarm's own spend counter on a false rollover; this is the whole file defaulting to a permissive number when it has no data at all. Note the script's OTHER fallback path (line 17, jq missing) emits allow 0 / human_active true -- i.e. the conservative default exists in the file and the no-data path does not use it. Cycle 47 declined the 10% and held at zero agents. Fix for a human: make ok:false imply allow 0, or carry the last known-good usage forward rather than zeroing it.
issues.note: CYCLE 48 CORROBORATION: the next real probe (ok:true, source:probe) reads allow_overall_pct 0 with weekly 95.0%, opus 97%, elapsed 87.4%, reserve 21.83. issues.status: open (repaired in the rendered artifact; the defective pattern is what remains filed)
issues.desc: CONDUCTOR-INSTRUMENT DEFECT, found at cycle 49 while rendering the dashboard. The LIVE per-target node in SWARM/runs/dashboard.html read "cycle 46 - 12 known issues open" while the run was at cycle 48. Cause: dashboard.html's first 112 lines are ONE HTML comment holding a legend with PLACEHOLDER copies of several live anchors, and runs/cycle47-dashboard.mjs matched the target node with /<div class="target"><b>\/opt\/targets\/aphorism-cli<\/b><span>[^<]*<\/span><\/div>/ -- no `g` flag and NO match-count assertion. String.replace with a non-global regex replaces only the FIRST match, and the first match in the file is the legend copy at line 38. So cycle 47 patched a comment nobody sees and left the human-visible node stale; cycle 48 reused the same script and repeated it. DISCRIMINATOR against "the render simply did not run": the legend copy WAS advanced to cycle 47 and then to cycle 48, so the writes landed -- they landed in the wrong region. This is precisely the KI-11 failure mode that runs/c46-dash.mjs's own header warns about in prose, three cycles before it happened; the warning existed and the assertion did not. REPAIRED IN THE ARTIFACT at cycle 49 (runs/c49-dash.mjs anchors the substitution on the `<!-- TARGETS -->` marker so it cannot reach the legend, and asserts an exact match count of 1 before replacing). WHAT REMAINS OPEN is the general defect: the dashboard is re-rendered by a hand-written per-cycle script, so the discipline is re-implemented from scratch every cycle and is only as good as the conductor's memory of it. A prose warning in one cycle's script does not carry to the next. Fix for a human: either strip the legend comment out of the published artifact, or give the anchors machine-distinguishable ids so a render cannot address the legend at all.
issues.note: Cost, stated honestly: two cycles of a stale status line on the one page a human actually looks at, while the run itself was healthy and every other live region (banner, timeline, evidence strip) updated correctly. Nothing about the PRODUCT was misreported; the run metadata was. Filed rather than treated as a one-off render slip because the same trap has now fired twice in a row after being documented once.
issues.note_cycle_50: SECOND REGION, FOUND BY AUDIT RATHER THAN BY LUCK, AND OLDER THAN THE FIRST. Cycle 49 repaired the per-target node and stopped there; cycle 50 ran the KI-11 comment-classifier over EVERY live region (runs/c50-dash-audit.mjs) and found the identical trap had also eaten the EVIDENCE STRIP. The live <pre class="evidence"> still carried CYCLE 42's content while the legend's placeholder copy carried cycle 48's - so renders 43 through 48 had been writing the verification evidence into an HTML comment for SEVEN cycles, and cycle 49 did not touch the region at all. Repaired in the artifact by runs/c50-dash.mjs, anchored BETWEEN the <!-- TARGETS --> and <!-- /TARGETS --> markers with an exact match-count assertion, and confirmed by re-running the audit after the render. WHAT THIS CHANGES ABOUT THE ISSUE: cycle 49 framed it as a per-cycle scripting slip that had fired twice. It is broader than that - the defect is that NOTHING asserts a render reached the live copy, so every region is exposed independently and each one fails silently on its own schedule. The durable repair is still a human's template edit (strip the legend from the published artifact, or give the live anchors machine-distinguishable ids); the cheap standing mitigation, which cost one script this cycle, is to RUN THE AUDIT AFTER EVERY RENDER and require every mandated region to report live=1.

issues.status: open by decision, not by neglect
issues.desc: The Attribution section's "every number here is a checked table row or a loud failure" invariant is over ASCII DIGITS only. Two spellings of a false count still pass green: an English number WORD ("Nine of those entries are rated HIGH." — the true count is 8), and a non-ASCII digit (U+FF19 FULLWIDTH NINE), since JavaScript \d without the /u flag is ASCII-only. issues.why_it_matters: NOT A REGRESSION, and that is measured rather than assumed: both cells are ALSO green on the pre-change arm, so neither hole was introduced and neither was ever covered. Evidence: .swarm/runs/cycle-002-gate-closing-out.txt, which runs exactly these two cells on both arms for this purpose. The comment in the test file was weakened from "EVERY number" to "EVERY number written in digits" so the file does not overclaim, which is the part that actually matters — an invariant stated wider than it holds is worse than a narrower true one.
issues.remedy: Not closed, and the argument against closing is the design's own: banning English number words in this section means banning "two".."twenty" while sparing "one", because the section's live, entirely true sentence ends "...says what would settle each one." A rule with a carve-out is the "no numbers, except..." shape this design exists to avoid, and the whole value of C7 is that it is one sentence a maintainer can hold in their head. The fullwidth-digit half is cheap (add /u and a Unicode digit class) and could be done independently if anyone judges the contrived case worth the line; it is not bundled here because closing half of a boundary and reporting the boundary closed is the failure mode this repo keeps guarding against.

issues.status: accepted trade, documented at the guard
issues.desc: C7 scans fenced code blocks, so a TRUE snippet in the Attribution section that carries a digit is rejected — e.g. `grep -c "| HIGH |" docs/corpus-attribution-triage.md   # 8`. Gate cell T7: green on the pre-change arm, RED on the fix. This is a new false rejection, deliberately bought.
issues.why_it_matters: What it buys is the closure of a silent hole: with fences excluded, a FALSE count inside a fence passed green (gate cell F5), and the code this change DELETED had caught that — so excluding fences was a genuine coverage regression, which is why attempt 1 was rejected. Traded on this repo's own standing precedent, recorded at cycle 30 of the previous run: a false rejection that is loud and has a named remedy beats a silent acceptance of a wrong claim, when those are the only two measured options. Both directions were measured here, so the trade is a choice between two knowns rather than a guess.
issues.remedy: None sought. If a maintainer needs a digit-bearing snippet in this section the remedies are both cheap and both named in the failure message: put the snippet in a section C7 does not police, or drop the digit from the comment. Reversing the trade means reopening the F5 hole and should not be done without re-running the cycle-2 gate.

issues.status: RESOLVED at cycle 7 of run #2 — measured against the commit the claim names
issues.desc: REPORT.md carries a LINE-COUNT claim family that nothing re-derives, and it drifts every time any test file changes. Three sites state "1511 of 2101 test lines" / "2101 lines of tests" (REPORT.md:155, :170, :440) against a measured 1978 of 3034. Unlike the corpus and triage counts — which the shipped suite asserts structurally, so they cannot go stale without turning the suite red — the line counts are asserted by nothing and are invisible to every guard in the repo. They were already false when cycle 4 began (run #2 s cycles 2 and 3 grew readme-tags.test.js by 467 lines) and J-4 s reconciliation sweep did not reach them.
issues.why_it_matters: It is the same structural complaint the run keeps arriving at from different directions: a number with no reader drifts silently. The corpus counts are safe because a test reads them; these are not read by anything, so the only thing standing between them and staleness is a human noticing. Small in itself — no user sees REPORT.md — but it is the doc a MAINTAINER is told to trust, which is audience #2 in SPEC.md.
issues.remedy: Two options, and the cheap one is probably right. (1) DELETE the line counts. They are decoration: no decision anywhere depends on knowing the test suite is 3034 lines rather than 2101, and the "1511 of 2101" framing was making a point about guard-family bloat that the J-2a/J-2b removals have since made obsolete. (2) Give them a reader — assert them from a test, the way the corpus counts are asserted — which is more machinery than the claim is worth and would add a guard whose only job is to police a number nobody needs. Option 1 is the lean. Either way it belongs to J-4 attempt 2, which is where the three sites are named.
issues.note_cycle_7_run2: CLOSED, and by measurement rather than by inheriting J-4's word. The three sites this issue named are all inside (or now point into) REPORT.md's "Fresh derivation table", which J-4 attempt 2 rebuilt with an explicit vintage: the preamble states "Everything below is measured at commit dbc1939", the value column is headed "Value at dbc1939", and the reader is told to re-run each command without the ref to get today's number. That converts the drifting claim family into checkable history. Re-derived at that commit this cycle, 9/9: args 217, cli 541, readme-tags 1978, select 298, total 3034; shipped source 549; suite 101 pass / 0 fail (measured by extracting the ref into a throwaway tree and running the project's own test_cmd). CONTROLS 2/2 LIVE — readme-tags is 2175 and the total 3231 at HEAD, so the gate demonstrably could have failed and did not. Evidence: .swarm/runs/cycle-007-verify-J-8.txt. The structural complaint this issue raised (a number with no reader drifts silently) is NOT withdrawn — it is answered here by pinning the numbers to a commit instead of by giving them a reader, which is the cheaper of the two remedies it proposed.

Effect is a paged human, never a stalled run. Two candidate fixes: raise HEALTH_STALE_MIN above the longest expected cycle, or key the suppression off the spawned session (heartbeat.ts moving) rather than off the service unit.

SWARM TOOL GAP, HIGH because it silently removes the run's crash-recovery net (morning report, not a live edit -- hard rule 5 fences bin/). THE WATCHDOG WAS INERT FOR THIS ENTIRE RUN. reference/cycle.md WRAP_UP step 6 specifies the DONE-guard as "wrap_up_complete OR <target>/REPORT.md existing in every target", with the file check as a safety net for a lost flag write. On an IMPROVEMENT run the target already carries a REPORT.md from the previous run, so that safety net is true from the first firing and the guard can never come false. MEASURED, not inferred: runs/watchdog.log shows decision=all-done detail=reports-present at EVERY firing from 09:05:10Z (30 min after the 08:34 kickoff) through 13:35:47Z -- ten consecutive firings across the whole live run. Had the conductor died mid-cycle, no relaunch would ever have been attempted. NO HARM MATERIALISED this run: on the VPS bin/swarm-pacer.sh is the firing mechanism and it spawned every cycle normally; the watchdog is the recovery path, and it is the recovery path that was missing. Composes badly with KI-25: the dead-man switch cried wolf twice during healthy work while the actual watchdog slept through the entire run. Candidate fix: the file half of the DONE-guard should require a REPORT.md newer than the runfile's run start (or carrying this run_label), not merely present.
issues.note_cycle_008_run3: SETTLED as a claim, still OPEN as a defect (it lives in SWARM/bin, which hard rule 5 fences from live edits). Backlog N-9 re-measured it on a SECOND run: 6 more all-done/reports-present firings, 04:09:47Z-06:39:49Z. NEW and stronger than the original record: the whole-history histogram of runs/watchdog.log is 150 all-done / 37 run-complete / 5 no-run / 3 fresh across 195 firings, with ZERO decision=relaunch EVER - so the relaunch path is not merely blocked on improvement runs, it has never once executed in any run. Source-confirmed: DONE-guard exit 0 at swarm-watchdog.sh:283, staleness gate at :340, never reached; watchdog.mode=normal so the pacer-mode skip at :344 is NOT a factor. Root cause credit stays with run #2 cycle 9, which already named the improvement-run REPORT.md collision - cycle 8 confirms and extends it, it did not discover it. Hand-off patch (mtime-gate the file check against run_started_at) and the one human decision it needs (mtime test vs an explicit improvement_run flag) are in .swarm/runs/cycle-008-N-9-watchdog-finding.md. BOUNDED: fixing the guard makes recovery REACHABLE, not PROVEN - a path with 0/195 executions still needs a drill, and that is a SMOKE-target job, never a live-run one.

issues.desc: README.md:10 claims a “Node 18+” support floor that nothing in this repo verifies. There is no package.json engines field, no CI matrix, and no runtime assertion; the claim is consistent with the node:test and require() usage but is not established by it. Measured at cycle 3 by N-7 and deliberately left untouched rather than guessed at.
issues.settles_it: Either run the suite under Node 18 and 20 and record the output, or replace the claim with the lowest version actually exercised. A CI matrix is the durable form.

issues.what: Repeated --tag / --author is unprotected AND spec-undecided. Shipped behaviour is last-occurrence-wins; the suite does not notice a first-wins implementation (102p/0f against the mutant, conductor-reproduced). SPEC describes every filter flag in the singular and never mentions repetition.
issues.settled_by: A human ruling in SPEC.md (tracked as J-7 item 3). Only once the behaviour is decided may a test pin it - hardening it now would freeze an artifact of argument-parsing order.

issues.what: Three domain-rule clauses (D-04 non-integer seeds, D-36 --help on stdout, D-41 positional-argument rejection) are each killed by exactly ONE test. A single test deletion or skip silently removes protection for that clause.
issues.settled_by: Either accept it explicitly, or add a second independent assertion per clause. Measured by N-4 at cycle 4 as a by-product; not itself a defect, but it is the thin ice in an otherwise 41/43-killed map.

issues.what: The SWARM self-modification fence (hard rule 5) depends on agent goodwill. The N-4 agent found /tmp blocked by its sandbox and created scratch at /opt/swarm/.n4-scratch - INSIDE the SWARM repo, outside the runs/ and playbook/ paths the fence permits. It was dispatched with target paths only and never told a SWARM path; it derived one. It cleaned up after itself (directory absent and git status clean at verification), so no residue reached the repo.
issues.settled_by: Give subagents a writable scratch dir inside the TARGET (e.g. <target>/.swarm/runs/scratch) in the dispatch contract, or unblock /tmp for subagents. Until then the fence is a convention, not a control.

issues.what: bin/aphorism.js writes to process.stdout (lines 28, 43, 48) with no error handler, so any stdout write failure surfaces as an unhandled 'error' event: ~1006 bytes of raw Node internals on stderr. Two measured instances. (a) EPIPE when a consumer closes the pipe without reading — `--list | true`, `| true`, `--list | head -0`, `--list | /nonexistent-cmd-xyz`. Realistic trigger: the downstream command fails to exec. (b) ENOSPC on a failed write exits 1, the code README documents as "no aphorism matched", so a script mistakes a full disk for an empty filter result. NOT triggered by consumers that read at least one line: head -1, head -5, sed 1q, grep -q and wc -l are all measured clean.
issues.settled_by: Backlog Q-1 (todo, priority 2). Handle stdout error events: exit quietly on EPIPE per Unix filter convention, and report other write failures in the tool's own one-line "aphorism: ..." convention with an exit code distinct from 1.
issues.resolution: RESOLVED by Q-1 (cycle 7, stdout) + Q-3 (cycle 8, stderr), and verified by RE-RUNNING KI-31 own two measured instances rather than by assuming the fixes covered them. (a) All four EPIPE reproducers it named - `| true`, `--list | true`, `--list | head -0`, `--list | /nonexistent-cmd-xyz` - now exit 0 with zero Node internals on stderr (KI-31 recorded ~1006 bytes of raw trace). (b) The ENOSPC instance, which KI-31 measured as exit 1 and therefore colliding with the documented no-match code, now exits 3 (EXIT_WRITE_ERROR) with the one-line `aphorism: ENOSPC: no space left on device, write`. Controls KI-31 listed as already-clean (head -1, wc -l) stay exit 0. Evidence: .swarm/runs/cycle-008-verify-Q-3.txt.

issues.what: The dashboard render harness (runs/c*-dashboard.mjs, used by cycles 3-6) substitutes the evidence block at the FIRST match of the evidence <pre> tag. dashboard.html holds three such blocks, two of them inside HTML template comments, and the FIRST is a commented one. The harness therefore reports "ok evidence block" and "MISS count: 0" while the live TARGETS-region block stays stale. Measured at cycle 6: lines 60 and 346 are commented, line 379 is live; only line 60 was being updated. A "zero MISS" render report is NOT evidence that the page a visitor sees is current. The same duplication hid a second staleness: the phase badge read BUILD through cycle 5 although the phase was REVIEW.
issues.settled_by: Either strip the template-comment copies from dashboard.html so exactly one evidence block exists, or make the harness select the block not enclosed in a comment and assert an EXPECTED occurrence count per anchor (it already prints counts for the other anchors, which is how the duplication became visible at all). Cycle 6 corrected the CONTENT by replacing every block still carrying the previous cycle tag, but the harness bug itself is untouched — hard rule 5 forbids editing SWARM tooling mid-run.

issues.what: SWARM-side cycle commits carry messages that assert contents the commits do not and cannot have. `runs/` is gitignored in the SWARM repo (.gitignore:2), so the dashboard, the per-cycle render harness and the runfile are ALL untracked there -- yet several run #3 commit subjects name exactly those three artifacts.
issues.detail: MEASURED at cycle 9, not inferred. `git -C /opt/swarm show --stat 76b3a01` -> subject "run #3 cycle 6: QA full pass -- dashboard render, c6 harness, runfile", contents: tmp_aph_err.txt (0 bytes) and tmp_aph_out.txt (0 bytes), 2 files changed, 0 insertions, 0 deletions. The commit contains two empty stray temp files and nothing else. The same shape applies to c2 (c2703b1). Found because cycle 9's own SWARM commit returned "nothing to commit, working tree clean" and that was CHECKED rather than shrugged off; `git check-ignore -v` confirmed runs/dashboard.html, runs/c9-dashboard.mjs and runs/current.json are all ignored by .gitignore:2.
issues.why_it_matters: Low severity because NOTHING IS LOST: the durable state lives in the TARGET repo, which is committed and pushed every cycle per hard rule 1 and carries .swarm/journal.md, state.json, backlog.json and every per-cycle artifact. The runfile is additionally mirrored into each journal block, which is exactly the RESUME path for a lost runfile. The defect is one of RECORD HONESTY, not data: a reader auditing the run through SWARM commit subjects would believe a dashboard render was committed there when it was not. It also means the gitignored `runs/` tree is the ONE part of the run with no version history -- a bad render overwrites the previous one irrecoverably.
issues.fix: Two independent halves, both for a human, neither applied (hard rule 5 fences SWARM outside runs/ and playbook/, and .gitignore is outside both). (1) Stop naming untracked artifacts in SWARM commit subjects -- or drop the SWARM-side cycle commit entirely, since the target commit is the one that carries the state. (2) Decide deliberately whether `runs/` should stay ignored; if the per-cycle harnesses and dashboards are meant to be auditable, un-ignore runs/*.mjs and runs/dashboard.html. Also worth deleting the two stray empty tmp_aph_*.txt files that DID get committed.

issues.title: cycle-NNN-* artifact names collide across runs in .swarm/runs/
issues.detail: Improvement runs restart the cycle counter at 1 while writing into the same .swarm/runs/ directory, so run #3 cycle 10 shares a filename namespace with run #1 cycle 10. Both generations of cycle-010-* are present today and NOTHING was overwritten -- verified by intact Aug 15 timestamps -- but only because this cycle's suffixes (gate-TS-4, probe, verify-TS-4-attemptN) differ from run #1's (await, dashboard, heartbeat, persist, verify-I-4b). A collision would be a silent overwrite that reads as an ordinary modification in the per-cycle commit diff.
issues.exposure: Bounded and recoverable: .swarm/runs/ IS version-controlled in the target repo (unlike SWARM/runs/, see KI-34), so an overwrite is recoverable from git history even though it is not visible as a collision.
issues.why_not_fixed: The naming convention lives in SWARM/reference/cycle.md, which hard rule 5 fences as read-only mid-run.
issues.candidate_fix: Prefix per-run (cycle-r3-010-<type>) or fold the run label into the directory (.swarm/runs/run-3/).
